currentContext.expansion: Astonea Labs manufactures from a single facility at Raipur Rani, Haryana, described as equipped with modern machinery, quality control systems and operational infrastructure supporting scalable manufacturing, and operated in accordance with applicable quality standards including WHO-GMP. The concrete expansion steps taken during FY 2025-26 were: (i) an SME IPO on the BSE SME Platform, listed 3 June 2025, raising Rs 37.66 Crore through a fresh issue of 27,90,000 equity shares at Rs 135 per share and taking paid-up equity capital from Rs 7.60 Crore to Rs 10.51 Crore; (ii) acquisition of an adjoining land parcel of approximately 1 Acre at Village Haripur, Tehsil Raipur Rani, District Panchkula, Haryana 134204 (Khasra Nos. 45//15/1(1-8) and 15/2(6-12)) for an aggregate consideration of Rs 2.00 Crore excluding stamp duty and incidental expenses, Sale Deed registered 13 February 2026, undertaken as part of the long-term expansion strategy and intended to facilitate enhancement of manufacturing capacity, plant operations and factory infrastructure; (iii) incorporation of Astonea LLC, a wholly-owned foreign subsidiary in Sheridan, Wyoming, USA, per Certificate of Incorporation dated 25 January 2026, subscribed to 100% of membership interests in cash, to carry on pharmaceuticals, food supplements and cosmetics business in the US and other international jurisdictions; and (iv) acquisition of approximately 25.74% of Damaira Pharmaceuticals Private Limited (an existing pharma business with an approximate turnover of Rs 82.48 Crore per its latest audited financial statements) for Rs 6.25 Crore - 52,00,000 equity shares at Rs 12.02 per share including premium - funded by reallocating unutilised IPO proceeds (Rs 8.08 Crore remained unutilised as on 26 February 2026; the variation constituted about 16.59% of total IPO proceeds), with shareholders having authorised a stake of up to 33.33% at the AGM of 27 December 2025. Looking forward, management names capacity and productivity upgrades at the Raipur Rani facility and the operationalisation of Astonea LLC as FY 2026-27 priorities, alongside a Bolivia export-registration programme funded out of IPO proceeds. No rupee capex budget, no commissioning date and no capacity number is attached to any of these forward plans in the routed text. Separately, a fire incident led to production activities at the affected unit being temporarily suspended as a precautionary measure, with restoration activities underway and the extent of damage to property, plant and machinery, inventories and other operational assets still being assessed.

risks.note: Named as the first Key Business Risk in the Enterprise Risk Management section and repeated in the MD&A threats list: 'The pharmaceutical sector is governed by stringent regulatory frameworks. Any changes in applicable regulations, compliance requirements, or industry standards may impact business operations.' The exposure is structural because the Company's ability to serve both domestic and export customers rests on its facility remaining WHO-GMP compliant, and because it is building a regulated-market export pipeline (including a Bolivia registration programme and a new US commercial entity) whose revenue depends on obtaining and holding product registrations. Mitigation is stated only as maintaining compliance, strengthening internal processes and monitoring regulatory developments.

risks.risk: Single-site manufacturing concentration, with a fire incident already having suspended production at the affected unit
risks.note: The MD&A describes one manufacturing facility, at Raipur Rani, Haryana, as the source of the entire pharmaceutical, nutraceutical, cosmeceutical and cosmetic portfolio, so there is no disclosed alternate site to absorb a disruption. The Board's Report records that following a fire incident 'production activities at the affected unit were temporarily suspended as a precautionary measure, and restoration activities are underway', with the Company still 'assessing the extent of damage to property, plant and machinery, inventories, and other operational assets'. Management states the incident has not materially impacted fundamental operations or going-concern status, but describes it as material enough to warrant disclosure in the financial statements. (The fire paragraph reaches me in the strategy_outlook bundle; it is absent from the routed risks_esg bundle.)

risks.risk: Intense competition and pricing pressure in pharmaceutical and cosmetic markets
risks.note: Listed both as an MD&A threat ('Intense competition in pharmaceutical and cosmetic sectors'; 'Pricing pressures in domestic and international markets') and as a Key Business Risk: 'The pharmaceutical industry is highly competitive, with continuous developments in products, pricing strategies, and market dynamics.' It bites hardest on a contract/third-party manufacturer whose customers can re-tender the work, and it is the direct counter-pressure to the 370-570 bps EBITDA margin recovery management is guiding to for FY 2026-27. Stated mitigation is brand development, portfolio expansion, quality focus and customer-centric strategies.

risks.risk: Raw material price volatility and availability, and supply-chain / logistics disruption
risks.note: The MD&A threats list names 'Volatility in prices and availability of raw materials' and 'Supply chain disruptions and logistics-related challenges' as distinct exposures, and the ERM section pairs supply chain with product quality: 'Maintaining consistent product quality and ensuring efficient supply chain management are critical to pharmaceutical operations.' For a formulations manufacturer this is a direct gross-margin and delivery-reliability exposure, and it is the input side of the margin recovery being guided to. Mitigation is stated as quality-driven processes, reliable partnerships, effective planning and continuous monitoring.

risks.risk: Execution risk on the international and multi-entity expansion programme
risks.note: The ERM section flags Business Expansion Risk explicitly: 'As the Company expands its presence across domestic and international markets, execution challenges, market entry requirements, and operational complexities may arise.' The concrete exposure is that the FY 2026-27 guidance framework rests on three unproven pillars - operationalising Astonea LLC (incorporated in Wyoming only in January 2026, with no operations, no subscribed share capital and no turnover as at the reporting date), new export geographies including the Bolivia registration programme, and operating leverage from the FY26 channel investment - none of which has a track record.

risks.risk: Margin dependence on an unproven payback from the FY 2025-26 investment cycle
risks.note: Management attributes the 615 bps EBITDA margin compression in FY 2025-26 to deliberate investment in the distribution channel, brand platform, regulatory infrastructure and customer-facing footprint, arguing these are 'foundational outlays rather than recurring cost overruns' whose 'full payback is expected to accrue from FY 2026-27 onward as the channel matures and operating leverage absorbs what was an investment year'. If channel partners do not move into the assumed steady-state contribution profile, the spend is structural cost rather than deferred return, and the guided margin recovery does not arrive.

Named directly in the MD&A threats list ('Foreign exchange fluctuations affecting export operations'). Structural because the growth plan deliberately increases the export share of the business - continued penetration across the USA, Guatemala, Peru, Iraq and Yemen, new registrations in Bolivia, and a US commercial subsidiary - so currency exposure rises with the strategy. No hedging policy is described in the routed text.

risks.risk: Financial and liquidity risk on a growth balance sheet
risks.note: Flagged as a Key Business Risk: 'Effective financial management is essential to support growth initiatives and maintain operational stability.' The Company has strengthened the position post-IPO (debt-to-equity improved to 0.36x from 1.32x, finance costs down 10.6% YoY), but it has also committed IPO proceeds to a minority stake rather than to operating assets, retained all profits with no dividend and no transfer to reserves, and is guiding to +45-55% revenue growth - which is working-capital hungry for a manufacturer. Stated mitigation is prudent financial planning, efficient resource allocation and continuous monitoring.

risks.risk: Technological change and shifting consumer preference across the cosmeceutical and nutraceutical portfolio
risks.note: The MD&A threats list names 'Technological changes and evolving consumer preferences'. This is a real portfolio risk for a company whose own-brand push (Glow Up, Regero, Avicel) and cosmeceutical/nutraceutical verticals sell into consumer categories where formulation fashion, e-commerce channel economics and brand preference turn over quickly - in contrast to the prescription-pharma side.
